Thought: Looking at the proton NMR spectrum, I can see a triplet at 1.29 ppm (3H) which is characteristic of a CH3 group, specifically an ethyl group (CH3-CH2-). This is confirmed by its coupling to the neighboring CH2 group which appears as a quartet at 4.30 ppm (2H). This pattern is typical of an ethyl ester (CH3-CH2-O-).

Let me also check the carbon NMR to confirm this interpretation.
Action: carbon_nmr_spectra
Action Input: {}

Thought: The carbon NMR confirms the presence of one CH3 group. The signal at 14.26 ppm is characteristic of a methyl group in an ethyl ester (CH3-CH2-O-), which correlates with the proton NMR data we saw. The signal at 61.10 ppm corresponds to the CH2 group of the ethyl ester. There are no other signals in the typical methyl region (around 15-30 ppm), confirming that there is only one methyl group in the molecule.
Final Answer: 1
